mission_10: Multilingual speech recognition is the task of transcribing speech in multiple languages using a single unified model, enabling deployment across diverse linguistic populations without maintaining separate models for each language. The key challenge is handling the vast diversity in phonetic inventories, writing systems, grammatical structures, and acoustic characteristics across languages while maintaining high accuracy for each. Language-conditioned models address this by incorporating language identity as an input signal, typically through language embeddings that are added to the audio features or decoder state, allowing the shared model parameters to adapt their behavior based on the target language. Code-switching detection identifies points in the audio where the speaker switches between languages, a common phenomenon in multilingual communities that poses unique challenges for ASR. The multilingual decoder uses a shared architecture with language-specific vocabulary mappings, enabling it to generate text in the appropriate writing system for each language. Evaluation requires computing Word Error Rate (WER) both overall and per-language to ensure the model performs well across all supported languages rather than favoring high-resource ones. In this mission, you will implement language embeddings, a language-conditioned encoder with self-attention, code-switching detection, a multilingual decoder, and per-language WER evaluation.
